topStories.title: 黑客组织ShinyHunters声称入侵美国联邦调查局，窃取特工及求职者数据
topStories.originalTitle: Hacking group ShinyHunters claims it breached the FBI, stole agents’ and applicants’ data
topStories.snippet: The theft of agents' personal information could present a major counterintelligence threat, where agents and their families are extorted into cooperating with a foreign government.
topStories.fullContent:
ShinyHunters, a prolific cybercriminal group known for large-scale data theft and extortion, says it has breached the FBI and stolen data on thousands of agents and applicants. The hackers made the claim on their dark web leak site, which TechCrunch reviewed, saying they had stolen “sensitive data on almost all FBI agents and individuals who filed an application with the FBI for a job.”

404 Media first reported on the breach after receiving a sample of the stolen names, home addresses, and phone numbers of FBI agents and their spouses, and verifying a portion of the stolen data against public records. The hackers say their hack is “not financially motivated,” and are demanding that the FBI remove a report that they say contains false allegations about the group.

The independent publication said the hackers breached an Oracle PeopleSoft server, often used by human resources and recruiters to store job applicants’ personal information, then pivoted to breach an Amazon-hosted government cloud storing the agents and applicants’ data.

ShinyHunters told the publication that they took terabytes of data but did not say what they would do with the information if the FBI does not take down its published report. The stolen data could present a major counterintelligence threat, in which hackers and overseas spies use the information to coerce or extort FBI agents and their families into cooperating with a foreign government.

The hackers reportedly defaced the FBI’s jobs site, which showed at the time of publication that the portal was “currently down for maintenance.” The site also said that the FBI’s special agent applicant portal was also down.

The FBI did not respond to a request for comment about the incident on Tuesday, and neither did the ShinyHunters hackers.

This is the second known breach of an FBI system this year after unidentified hackers broke into one of the agency’s systems for managing real-time wiretaps and foreign intelligence-gathering warrants, which could have identified targets of the agency’s surveillance. Separately, FBI director Kash Patel also had his personal email account hacked and leaked by an Iran-backed hacking group called Handala in retaliation for U.S.-led strikes against Iran.

topStories.title: A16z通过创办学校，挑战硅谷对辍学生的偏爱
topStories.originalTitle: A16z is challenging Silicon Valley’s love for drop-outs by launching a school
topStories.snippet: This academy for promising high school grads is somewhere between a trade-school, Y Combinator and Peter Thiel's Fellowship Program.
topStories.fullContent:
Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz is launching a school called The Horowitz Andreessen Academy aimed at aspiring founders who have just graduated high school and have not yet attended college.

The academy is aiming to train these high school grads with hands-on coursework on a variety of topics ranging from the technical (such as “AI Research and Models”) to life philosophy (such as “The Geometry of Luck,” which promises to teach students “about arranging a life so good fortune flows through it.”) Students will also work on personal projects. The school’s main pitch is that it promises to provide students with mentors who are big names in tech.

The school is currently accepting applications for its first year, which will be a one-year program that charges no tuition, and is open to about 50 students, “chosen on proof of work: what they have built, shipped, or earned,” according to the school’s FAQ. The academy is located in San Francisco and students will be responsible for their own housing (although the school is working to help them find it and match them with other student roommates).

One item to note: the academy is currently not an accredited school, so participates will not earn a degree, or college credits that transfer elsewhere.

In 2028, The Horowitz Andreessen Academy — which is a for-profit venture that has raised $42 million — hopes to offer a two-year program. At that point, it plans to charge tuition “similar in cost to an elite private university,” the school’s CEO Gagan Biyani said in a post on X.

In exchange for that elite-tuition price tag, students will gain access to 200 speakers and mentors, including people from ten founding corporate partners: Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe. Those companies and dozens of others hope to hire from the grads of this school, Biyani said.

So, this is like if Y Combinator (the most famed startup school) and Peter Thiel’s Fellowship Program (a famed program for young people who opt to build companies instead of attend college) had a baby. The difference is, instead of a short-term experience ending with funding for a company, these students will pay tuition, earn tech-trade skills and have an inside track at tech industry jobs. Or they may also have a startup in the works, built with access to a lot of mentorship.

As the founders of the academy describe, it’s meant to be a new, middle ground between obtaining a full degree before entering the tech industry and dropping out to start a company. In this era where AI has been hampering the entry-level job market, gaining access to jobs may enough reason for some young people to try this new trade-school like approach.

风险投资公司安德森·霍洛维茨（Andreessen Horowitz）正在创办一所名为“霍洛维茨·安德森学院”（The Horowitz Andreessen Academy）的学校，面向刚刚高中毕业、尚未上大学的创业者候选人。

该学院旨在通过涵盖多个领域的实践课程培训这些高中毕业生，课程范围从技术类主题（如“人工智能研究与模型”）到人生哲学类主题（如“幸运的几何学”——该课程承诺教会学生“如何安排一种生活，让好运流经其中”）。学生还将开展个人项目。该校的核心卖点是承诺为学生提供科技行业知名人士担任导师。

该校目前正在招收首届学生。第一届为期一年，不收学费，面向约50名学生开放。根据学校常见问题页面的说法，学生将“依据工作成果进行选拔：看他们构建、发布或赚取了什么”。学院位于旧金山，学生需自行解决住宿问题，不过学校正努力帮助他们寻找住处，并为他们与其他学生匹配合租室友。

需要注意的是：该学院目前尚未获得认证，因此参与者不会获得学位，也不会获得可转入其他院校的大学学分。

霍洛维茨·安德森学院是一家营利性企业，已筹集4200万美元。学院希望在2028年开设为期两年的项目。届时，学校计划收取“费用水平类似于顶尖私立大学”的学费。该校首席执行官加甘·比亚尼（Gagan Biyani）在X平台发帖称。

作为这笔精英高校级别学费的交换，学生将获得接触200名演讲嘉宾和导师的机会，其中包括来自十家创始企业合作伙伴的人员：安杜里尔（Anduril）、Anthropic、Coinbase、谷歌、Meta、英伟达、OpenAI、Palantir、Replit和Stripe。比亚尼说，这些公司以及其他数十家公司都希望从该校毕业生中招聘人才。

因此，这所学校就像是Y Combinator（最知名的创业学校）和彼得·蒂尔奖学金项目（一个知名项目，面向选择创办公司而非上大学的年轻人）的结合体。不同之处在于，这些学生不是参加一个以获得公司融资为终点的短期项目，而是要支付学费、学习科技行业的职业技能，并获得进入科技行业就业的优先机会。当然，他们也可能已经在筹备一家初创公司，并在大量导师资源的支持下推进创业。

正如学院创始人所描述的那样，该校意在成为两条路径之间的新型中间地带：一条是在进入科技行业前先获得完整学位，另一条则是辍学创业。在人工智能阻碍入门级就业市场的当下，对一些年轻人来说，获得工作机会本身可能就足以成为尝试这种类似职业学校模式的新途径的理由。

topStories.fullContent:
Providing psychological safety to Black, Asian and ethnic minority staff so they can raise concerns about patient care without fear would save lives, write Dr Jennifer Creese, Dr Joy Spiliopoulos and Prof Carolyn Tarrant

Your report ( One in five black, Asian and minority ethnic NHS managers in England plan to quit amid racism, report finds, 15 September ) rightly highlights racism, exclusion and blocked career progression in the NHS. But it also points to a wider risk: patient safety. Care mistakes already cost the NHS £14.7bn a year .

A March 2025 report by the NHS Race & Health Observatory notes that Black, Asian and minority ethnic (BAME) staff, who make up more than 40% of the medical and dental workforce, still face harassment and discrimination in promotion, everyday work and disciplinary processes. This fuels stress, burnout and poorer mental health. Bullying and harassment are estimated to cost NHS England £2bn a year through staff turnover, sickness and lost productivity. In such environments, BAME staff are less likely than white colleagues to speak up about patient safety, fearing that their concerns will not be understood or taken seriously.
topStories.fullTranslation:
詹妮弗·克里斯博士（Dr Jennifer Creese）、乔伊·斯皮利奥普洛斯博士（Dr Joy Spiliopoulos）和卡罗琳·塔兰特教授（Prof Carolyn Tarrant）写道，为黑人、亚裔和少数族裔员工提供心理安全保障，使他们能够毫无畏惧地提出对患者护理的担忧，将挽救生命。

贵报的报道（《报告发现：在英格兰，五分之一的黑人、亚裔及少数族裔NHS管理者因种族主义计划辞职》，9月15日）准确指出了英国国家医疗服务体系（NHS）内部存在的种族主义、排斥以及职业发展受阻问题。但这同时也指向了一个更广泛的风险：患者安全。医疗差错每年已给NHS造成高达147亿英镑的损失。

NHS种族与健康观察机构（NHS Race & Health Observatory）2025年3月的一份报告指出，在医疗和牙科从业人员中占比超过40%的黑人、亚裔和少数族裔（BAME）员工，在晋升、日常工作以及纪律处分程序中仍面临骚扰与歧视。这加剧了心理压力、职业倦怠以及较差的心理健康状况。据估计，欺凌和骚扰通过导致人员流失、病假和生产力下降，每年给英格兰NHS造成20亿英镑的损失。在这样的环境下，少数族裔员工比白人同事更不愿意公开谈论患者安全问题，他们担心自己的关切不会被理解或受到重视。

topStories.fullContent: India’s imports of Russian crude fell 16.5% in August and are expected to decline again in September, just as a new U.S. sanctions law gives Washington authority to hit major Russian oil buyers with tariffs of up to 100%. Russian shipments to India dropped to about 2.1 million barrels per day in August from July’s record levels, according to trade data cited by Reuters. Preliminary Kpler data puts September imports at 1.9 million bpd. Russia remains India’s largest crude supplier. The August decline predates the new U.S. law, so calling it a sanctions retreat would be a stretch. Indian refiners were already shifting barrels around as Middle Eastern supply routes improved. Purchases of Iraqi crude jumped roughly 25% to 171,000 bpd in August. Saudi imports rose 1.5% to 328,000 bpd. UAE shipments fell 5.4% to 620,000 bpd, although ADNOC has expanded its ability to move crude from inside Hormuz to export points outside the strait. India’s total crude imports fell 8.8% in August to 4.44 million bpd. October and November buying could tell a different story. Indian refiners are tapping spot markets for replacement barrels as they weigh the risk attached to future Russian purchases. President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act on Friday, giving the administration authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods from qualifying major buyers of Russian energy. The law does not automatically impose those tariffs. India also has a very expensive reason to shop carefully. Its crude import bill jumped 48.4% year over year to $74.8 billion between April and August even though import volumes slipped 0.4%. Higher crude prices and freight costs have eaten away at the savings India spent years extracting from discounted Russian barrels. Russian crude still makes economic sense for Indian refiners, but the calculation gets considerably uglier if the discount on the oil comes attached to a potential tariff on everything else India sells to the United States. By Julianne Geiger for Oilprice.com

topStories.originalTitle: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna, boasting lower cost and fewer mistakes
topStories.snippet: OpenAI is launching two new models, which it says are cut from the same cloth as Astra.
topStories.fullContent:
Earlier this month, OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra, which it heralded as its most powerful and capable model yet, and the “world’s best model” for a variety of activities, including computer work and coding. Now, the lab is expanding the GPT-6 generation with updated versions of the smaller Sol and Luna models.

“GPT-6 Astra introduced a new generation of intelligence; these models extend its benefits by making that intelligence more efficient and accessible,” the company writes.

The first models in the Sol and Luna series were introduced earlier this year, representing different tiers in OpenAI’s hierarchy of models. Sol is designed for complex tasks like coding, while OpenAI says Luna is more appropriate for clerical work — “high-volume tasks with a clear goal, like summarizing documents, extracting information, or answering quick questions.”

OpenAI is also emphasizing big improvements in efficiency and affordability — most notably, via a substantial price drop for API access. The 6 series models will be available at half the cost of the 5.6 series of Sol and Luna, a price drop that OpenAI attributes to improvements in caching and inference.

OpenAI also claims that its newest models are better at producing answers that are factually accurate, and notes that they have a lower error rate when it comes to coding.

“On our internal factuality evaluation, which is based on de-identified real-world conversations where users flagged mistakes by our models, GPT-6 Sol makes about half as many mistakes as its predecessor, reaching Astra-level reliability at much lower cost,” the announcement reads.

As is typical with OpenAI’s new model releases, the company is claiming that its newest offerings outshine those of its primary competitor, Anthropic. The company repeatedly claims that GPT-6 Sol and Luna handle tasks substantially better than Anthropic’s top models — like Fable and Opus.

Notably, Anthropic released a new version of Opus 5.5 just 90 minutes before OpenAI’s release, reflecting the intense competition between the two companies.

The new versions of Sol and Luna are now available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for most paid accounts, and in the ChatGPT API, while Luna will be available in the desktop app and for Free and Go users. OpenAI expects to roll out the models to ChatGPT (the app and website) gradually throughout the day.

See All by Gaby Del Valle

San Francisco is suing the Trump Media & Technology Group, the parent company behind Truth Social, for selling early access to President Donald Trump’s posts on the social media site. The lawsuit, filed today in California state court, alleges that the Truth API feed is a “corrupt business scheme” that violates both California’s Unfair Competition Law and federal ethics and anti-corruption laws that prohibit insider trading.

White House spokesperson Davis Ingle recently called Truth Social the “most powerful and popular social media platform in the world.” While the latter part of that statement is objectively untrue based on any credible estimates — in fact, Truth Social traffic has declined over the last year — Trump often makes high-stakes announcements in his capacity as president on the platform, and his posts there have a clear effect on the global economy. To capitalize on this, Trump Media recently launched Truth API, a service that charges select customers $100,000 a month for early access to the 10 most influential accounts on Truth Social, including Trump’s and those of other White House officials. Trump Media’s interim CEO, Kevin McGurn, acknowledged as much in his announcement of Truth API, saying that “markets already move on Truth Social posts.”

The San Francisco lawsuit cites several examples of this, some of which took place after the launch of Truth API. On August 21st, for example, Trump posted that the federal government was going to “lower the price of ground beef for working families” by exempting some ground beef imports from tariffs. When the market opened a few hours later, cattle futures declined significantly, according to the complaint.

In today’s markets, early access means millions of dollars. This business scheme has turned public trust into private property.

“Trump Media has unlawfully created, priced, marketed, and operated a commercial mechanism that knowingly and willfully facilitates Trump’s use of nonpublic information for private profit,” the complaint alleges. The San Francisco suit alleges that Truth API is a way of making the floundering Trump Media — which reported a net loss of more than $238 million earlier this year — profitable.

Per his agreement with Trump Media, Truth Social has a six-hour exclusivity window on Trump’s posts, meaning he can’t post the same material elsewhere in that time frame. Even before the launch of Truth API, Trump’s Truth Social profile was extremely valuable for investors — so valuable that the company has sought to capitalize on it. The San Francisco complaint cites reports of hedge fund executives who say they feel pressured to buy the service even though they think it’s legally risky. “It’s a pay-to-play scheme for early access to the president’s market-moving government statements,” San Francisco city attorney David Chiu said in a Tuesday press conference. “In today’s markets, early access means millions of dollars. This business scheme has turned public trust into private property.” Beyond violating insider trading laws, the suit claims, Truth API disadvantages everyday investors by paywalling financially valuable information.

Trump Media hasn’t disclosed its list of Truth API clients, but the company has said it plans on marketing the product to AI companies and large news organizations.

The city has asked a judge to forbid Trump Media from offering Truth API or similar services, and to impose a fine of $2,500 per violation of California’s Unfair Competition Law.

This isn’t the first time Trump has been sued over Truth API. In August, The Intercept and the Freedom of the Press Foundation filed a joint lawsuit in a New York federal court over the product, which it called “extraordinary, corrupt, and unconstitutional.”

旧金山市正起诉特朗普媒体与科技集团（Trump Media & Technology Group），即社交平台Truth Social背后的母公司，原因是该公司出售总统唐纳德·特朗普在这一社交媒体网站上所发布帖文的提前获取权限。这起诉讼于今天在加利福尼亚州法院提起，指控Truth API信息流是一项“腐败的商业计划”，既违反加州《不正当竞争法》，也违反禁止内幕交易的联邦道德和反腐败法律。

白宫发言人戴维斯·英格尔最近称Truth Social是“世界上最强大、最受欢迎的社交媒体平台”。然而，根据任何可信的估算，后半句说法在客观上并不属实——事实上，Truth Social的流量在过去一年有所下降。但特朗普经常以总统身份在该平台上发布具有重大影响力的消息，而他在那里发布的帖子显然会对全球经济产生影响。为了从中获利，特朗普媒体公司最近推出了Truth API。这项服务每月向特定客户收取10万美元，让他们提前获取Truth Social上影响力最大的10个账户的内容，其中包括特朗普以及其他白宫官员的账户。特朗普媒体公司的临时首席执行官凯文·麦格恩在宣布Truth API时也承认了这一点，他说：“市场已经会因Truth Social上的帖子而波动。”

旧金山的诉讼列举了多个相关例子，其中一些发生在Truth API推出之后。例如，8月21日，特朗普发帖称，联邦政府将通过免除部分碎牛肉进口产品的关税，来“降低工薪家庭购买碎牛肉的价格”。诉状称，几小时后市场开盘时，牛类期货价格大幅下跌。

在如今的市场中，提前获取信息意味着数百万美元。这项商业计划把公众信任变成了私人财产。

诉状称：“特朗普媒体公司非法创设、定价、营销并运营了一种商业机制，明知并故意促成特朗普利用非公开信息谋取私利。”旧金山方面的诉讼称，Truth API旨在让陷入困境的特朗普媒体公司实现盈利；该公司今年早些时候公布的净亏损超过2.38亿美元。

根据特朗普媒体公司与特朗普达成的协议，Truth Social对特朗普的帖子拥有6小时的独家发布窗口，这意味着特朗普在这段时间内不能在其他地方发布相同内容。即使在Truth API推出之前，特朗普的Truth Social个人资料对投资者而言就已极具价值——价值之高，以至于该公司一直在寻求从中获利。旧金山的诉状援引了对冲基金高管的相关报道，这些高管表示，尽管认为购买这项服务存在法律风险，他们仍感到有压力必须购买。旧金山市检察官戴维·丘在周二的新闻发布会上说：“这是一个花钱购买提前获取总统具有市场影响力的政府声明权限的交易计划。在如今的市场中，提前获取信息意味着数百万美元。这项商业计划把公众信任变成了私人财产。”诉讼称，Truth API不仅违反内幕交易法，还通过对具有金融价值的信息设置付费墙，使普通投资者处于不利地位。

特朗普媒体公司尚未披露Truth API客户名单，但该公司表示，计划向人工智能公司和大型新闻机构营销这款产品。

旧金山市已请求法官禁止特朗普媒体公司提供Truth API或类似服务，并针对每一项违反加州《不正当竞争法》的行为处以2500美元罚款。

这并不是特朗普第一次因Truth API遭到起诉。今年8月，《拦截》（The Intercept）和新闻自由基金会（Freedom of the Press Foundation）曾在纽约一家联邦法院就这项产品联合提起诉讼，称该产品“非同寻常、腐败且违宪”。

topStories.title: Waymo最新扩张策略：青少年
topStories.snippet: Waymo is opening its robotaxi service to teenagers aged 13 to 17 in Nashville, its second city to offer rides to minors.
topStories.fullContent:
Waymo will allow teenagers as young as 13 to use its robotaxi service in Nashville as the Alphabet-owned company looks to scale its business by reaching a new group of riders.

Nashville is the second city to offer Waymo teen accounts; the company kicked off its teen account program in Phoenix last year. And more cities are likely to follow, according to the company.

A Waymo spokesperson told TechCrunch that its expansion to Nashville will be the “first of many” teen launches across multiple markets that use the Waymo app in the coming months. The spokesperson said it will offer teen accounts in cities where its operations are mature and local regulations allow it.

Nashville is a relatively new market for Waymo, although it has support from local leaders to offer the service to teens. The company launched its service in a 50-square-mile area of Nashville in April 2026, and earlier this month, its robotaxis became available on the Lyft app.

Waymo’s ridership has skyrocketed over the past two years — a trajectory largely driven by the rapid succession of new markets. Paid robotaxi trips grew tenfold from 50,000 per week in May 2024 to more than half-a-million per week earlier this year. Over that same time span, Waymo has launched robotaxi services in a dozen cities. In the past month alone, the company opened robotaxi services in Denver, Las Vegas, San Diego, and Tampa.

The company’s introduction of teen accounts provides another means of growth — this one targeted at a demographic that relies on parents or public transit to get to school, work, or activities.

There are few limits to the service. The teen account must be connected to a parent or guardian, but once activated, teens can hail autonomous rides anywhere in Waymo’s service area in Nashville — and bring their friends along. Waymo told TechCrunch that teen account holders can bring up to three guests ages 13 to 17. The company didn’t share how these ages would be verified.

That kind of access could certainly invite chaos — it’s not hard to imagine four 16-year-old kids unleashed in a robotaxi. But it may also be part of the appeal for parents who would rather their kids pile into a Waymo than in a vehicle driven by a teenager.

The Horowitz Andreessen Academy trades degrees and homework for stints at tech companies.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Emma Roth

Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) is creating an “academy” positioned as a pipeline for young people to build or join a Silicon Valley startup. The “Horowitz Andreessen Academy” will launch with 10 partners, including Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe, along with $42 million in funding led by a16z. While billed as a “highly selective school,” it does not grant any degree or accreditation. Instead, students will attend short classes led by tech figureheads, like OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, as well as “co-ops” that give students roles at tech companies.

To partake in the one-year program, students will have to move to San Francisco and arrange their own housing, according to the academy’s FAQ page. Students are promised more than $50,000 in compute credits and a $5,000 travel and research budget offered by a16z. The announcement says they’ll have “no traditional grades, tests, or homework,” but will “learn from Silicon Valley’s most storied founders and operators in short, high-impact classes and spend the rest of your time working and exploring.”

The academy seems like the latest attempt by Silicon Valley’s billionaires to “fix” America’s education system by creating their own. Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Jeff Bezos have all poured money into starting their own schools, while a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz have been critical of colleges. Last year, Andreessen reportedly called Stanford and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology “political lobbying operations fighting American innovation” in a group chat with White House officials and tech leaders, according to The Washington Post.

The Horowitz Andreessen Academy will be free for its first one-year program in the fall of 2027. It will only accept 50 students and is designed mainly for recent high school graduates.

topStories.fullContent:
Anthropic’s newest model, Opus 5.5, was released on Tuesday, setting a new state-of-the-art in coding and knowledge work performance, according to the company. Opus is the most capable and expensive tier in Anthropic’s three-tier Claude lineup; Sonnet sits in the middle, while Haiku is the fastest and cheapest. Notably, Anthropic says, the release outpaces the larger Fable model in many benchmarks and succeeded in a number of informal tasks that Fable failed to complete.

The new model is also significantly cheaper than its predecessor. Output tokens will be charged at $20 per million tokens for Opus 5.5, compared to $25 for the previous model. Other metrics have similar price drops. The model is also faster to run, reflecting an overall drop in the compute required to serve it.

The new version also makes significant changes to how Opus communicates, with the Opus 5.5 less likely to use jargon and more likely to put important information at the start of its messages.

The launch comes just two months after the release of Opus 5 on July 24. According to the announcement, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, which are the next tiers in the lineup, will be released “in the coming weeks,” with similar performance improvements.

Anthropic says that Opus 5.5 is comparable to Mythos in its biology and cybersecurity capabilities, so its release is subject to the same safeguards as the company’s Fable model. Those safeguards limit how much the models can be used to discover exploits in compiled programs or developing recognizable biological weapons, among other tasks.

Opus 5.5 is Anthropic’s first model release since CEO Dario Amodei embraced calls to pace the frontier, deliberately slowing down progress on AI capabilities to match the rate of progress on alignment.

“I have become convinced that fully addressing the risks requires even more prudence,” Amodei wrote in a post earlier this month, “not just investing in risk prevention, but pacing the rate of capabilities advancement so that risk prevention has time to keep up.”

Opus 5.5’s safety training was broadly similar to its predecessors, with alignment testing and pre-release evaluation by outside organizations like METR and Frontier Design. But Anthropic emphasized that more advanced training and evaluation systems were already being prepared for future models, including improved security and monitoring systems.

“As AI becomes more capable, public policy should play a larger role in making sure the systems people rely on are safe. That capacity takes time to build, and we’ve started to put the infrastructure in place to support it,” the blog post reads. “We expect to share more details on these efforts soon.”

UNITED NATIONS, September 22. /TASS/. US President Donald Trump believes he and Russian leader Vladimir Putin may hold another face-to-face meeting soon, but it is unlikely to take place at the upcoming G20 summit near Miami, Florida.

Reporters asked Trump about the prospects for a trilateral meeting with Vladimir Zelensky at the G20 summit. "Well, I don't know. I know that he [Putin] will meet, and we've had a meeting already in Alaska. I think he'd do another one. I don't know about Miami," Trump replied.

The G20 summit will take place on December 14-15 in Doral near Miami.

financeStories.fullContent: India’s imports of Russian crude fell 16.5% in August and are expected to decline again in September, just as a new U.S. sanctions law gives Washington authority to hit major Russian oil buyers with tariffs of up to 100%. Russian shipments to India dropped to about 2.1 million barrels per day in August from July’s record levels, according to trade data cited by Reuters. Preliminary Kpler data puts September imports at 1.9 million bpd. Russia remains India’s largest crude supplier. The August decline predates the new U.S. law, so calling it a sanctions retreat would be a stretch. Indian refiners were already shifting barrels around as Middle Eastern supply routes improved. Purchases of Iraqi crude jumped roughly 25% to 171,000 bpd in August. Saudi imports rose 1.5% to 328,000 bpd. UAE shipments fell 5.4% to 620,000 bpd, although ADNOC has expanded its ability to move crude from inside Hormuz to export points outside the strait. India’s total crude imports fell 8.8% in August to 4.44 million bpd. October and November buying could tell a different story. Indian refiners are tapping spot markets for replacement barrels as they weigh the risk attached to future Russian purchases. President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act on Friday, giving the administration authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on goods from qualifying major buyers of Russian energy. The law does not automatically impose those tariffs. India also has a very expensive reason to shop carefully. Its crude import bill jumped 48.4% year over year to $74.8 billion between April and August even though import volumes slipped 0.4%. Higher crude prices and freight costs have eaten away at the savings India spent years extracting from discounted Russian barrels. Russian crude still makes economic sense for Indian refiners, but the calculation gets considerably uglier if the discount on the oil comes attached to a potential tariff on everything else India sells to the United States. By Julianne Geiger for Oilprice.com

financeStories.originalTitle: Hacking group ShinyHunters claims it breached the FBI, stole agents’ and applicants’ data
financeStories.snippet: The theft of agents' personal information could present a major counterintelligence threat, where agents and their families are extorted into cooperating with a foreign government.
financeStories.fullContent:
ShinyHunters, a prolific cybercriminal group known for large-scale data theft and extortion, says it has breached the FBI and stolen data on thousands of agents and applicants. The hackers made the claim on their dark web leak site, which TechCrunch reviewed, saying they had stolen “sensitive data on almost all FBI agents and individuals who filed an application with the FBI for a job.”

404 Media first reported on the breach after receiving a sample of the stolen names, home addresses, and phone numbers of FBI agents and their spouses, and verifying a portion of the stolen data against public records. The hackers say their hack is “not financially motivated,” and are demanding that the FBI remove a report that they say contains false allegations about the group.

The independent publication said the hackers breached an Oracle PeopleSoft server, often used by human resources and recruiters to store job applicants’ personal information, then pivoted to breach an Amazon-hosted government cloud storing the agents and applicants’ data.

ShinyHunters told the publication that they took terabytes of data but did not say what they would do with the information if the FBI does not take down its published report. The stolen data could present a major counterintelligence threat, in which hackers and overseas spies use the information to coerce or extort FBI agents and their families into cooperating with a foreign government.

The hackers reportedly defaced the FBI’s jobs site, which showed at the time of publication that the portal was “currently down for maintenance.” The site also said that the FBI’s special agent applicant portal was also down.

The FBI did not respond to a request for comment about the incident on Tuesday, and neither did the ShinyHunters hackers.

This is the second known breach of an FBI system this year after unidentified hackers broke into one of the agency’s systems for managing real-time wiretaps and foreign intelligence-gathering warrants, which could have identified targets of the agency’s surveillance. Separately, FBI director Kash Patel also had his personal email account hacked and leaked by an Iran-backed hacking group called Handala in retaliation for U.S.-led strikes against Iran.

financeStories.title: A16z通过创办学校，挑战硅谷对辍学生的偏爱
financeStories.originalTitle: A16z is challenging Silicon Valley’s love for drop-outs by launching a school
financeStories.snippet: This academy for promising high school grads is somewhere between a trade-school, Y Combinator and Peter Thiel's Fellowship Program.
financeStories.fullContent:
Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz is launching a school called The Horowitz Andreessen Academy aimed at aspiring founders who have just graduated high school and have not yet attended college.

The academy is aiming to train these high school grads with hands-on coursework on a variety of topics ranging from the technical (such as “AI Research and Models”) to life philosophy (such as “The Geometry of Luck,” which promises to teach students “about arranging a life so good fortune flows through it.”) Students will also work on personal projects. The school’s main pitch is that it promises to provide students with mentors who are big names in tech.

The school is currently accepting applications for its first year, which will be a one-year program that charges no tuition, and is open to about 50 students, “chosen on proof of work: what they have built, shipped, or earned,” according to the school’s FAQ. The academy is located in San Francisco and students will be responsible for their own housing (although the school is working to help them find it and match them with other student roommates).

One item to note: the academy is currently not an accredited school, so participates will not earn a degree, or college credits that transfer elsewhere.

In 2028, The Horowitz Andreessen Academy — which is a for-profit venture that has raised $42 million — hopes to offer a two-year program. At that point, it plans to charge tuition “similar in cost to an elite private university,” the school’s CEO Gagan Biyani said in a post on X.

In exchange for that elite-tuition price tag, students will gain access to 200 speakers and mentors, including people from ten founding corporate partners: Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe. Those companies and dozens of others hope to hire from the grads of this school, Biyani said.

So, this is like if Y Combinator (the most famed startup school) and Peter Thiel’s Fellowship Program (a famed program for young people who opt to build companies instead of attend college) had a baby. The difference is, instead of a short-term experience ending with funding for a company, these students will pay tuition, earn tech-trade skills and have an inside track at tech industry jobs. Or they may also have a startup in the works, built with access to a lot of mentorship.

As the founders of the academy describe, it’s meant to be a new, middle ground between obtaining a full degree before entering the tech industry and dropping out to start a company. In this era where AI has been hampering the entry-level job market, gaining access to jobs may enough reason for some young people to try this new trade-school like approach.

该学院旨在通过涵盖多个领域的实践课程培训这些高中毕业生，课程范围从技术类主题（如“人工智能研究与模型”）到人生哲学类主题（如“幸运的几何学”——该课程承诺教会学生“如何安排一种生活，让好运流经其中”）。学生还将开展个人项目。该校的核心卖点是承诺为学生提供科技行业知名人士担任导师。

该校目前正在招收首届学生。第一届为期一年，不收学费，面向约50名学生开放。根据学校常见问题页面的说法，学生将“依据工作成果进行选拔：看他们构建、发布或赚取了什么”。学院位于旧金山，学生需自行解决住宿问题，不过学校正努力帮助他们寻找住处，并为他们与其他学生匹配合租室友。

需要注意的是：该学院目前尚未获得认证，因此参与者不会获得学位，也不会获得可转入其他院校的大学学分。

霍洛维茨·安德森学院是一家营利性企业，已筹集4200万美元。学院希望在2028年开设为期两年的项目。届时，学校计划收取“费用水平类似于顶尖私立大学”的学费。该校首席执行官加甘·比亚尼（Gagan Biyani）在X平台发帖称。

作为这笔精英高校级别学费的交换，学生将获得接触200名演讲嘉宾和导师的机会，其中包括来自十家创始企业合作伙伴的人员：安杜里尔（Anduril）、Anthropic、Coinbase、谷歌、Meta、英伟达、OpenAI、Palantir、Replit和Stripe。比亚尼说，这些公司以及其他数十家公司都希望从该校毕业生中招聘人才。

因此，这所学校就像是Y Combinator（最知名的创业学校）和彼得·蒂尔奖学金项目（一个知名项目，面向选择创办公司而非上大学的年轻人）的结合体。不同之处在于，这些学生不是参加一个以获得公司融资为终点的短期项目，而是要支付学费、学习科技行业的职业技能，并获得进入科技行业就业的优先机会。当然，他们也可能已经在筹备一家初创公司，并在大量导师资源的支持下推进创业。

正如学院创始人所描述的那样，该校意在成为两条路径之间的新型中间地带：一条是在进入科技行业前先获得完整学位，另一条则是辍学创业。在人工智能阻碍入门级就业市场的当下，对一些年轻人来说，获得工作机会本身可能就足以成为尝试这种类似职业学校模式的新途径的理由。

Providing psychological safety to Black, Asian and ethnic minority staff so they can raise concerns about patient care without fear would save lives, write Dr Jennifer Creese, Dr Joy Spiliopoulos and Prof Carolyn Tarrant

Your report ( One in five black, Asian and minority ethnic NHS managers in England plan to quit amid racism, report finds, 15 September ) rightly highlights racism, exclusion and blocked career progression in the NHS. But it also points to a wider risk: patient safety. Care mistakes already cost the NHS £14.7bn a year .

financeStories.fullContent:
Earlier this month, OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra, which it heralded as its most powerful and capable model yet, and the “world’s best model” for a variety of activities, including computer work and coding. Now, the lab is expanding the GPT-6 generation with updated versions of the smaller Sol and Luna models.

“GPT-6 Astra introduced a new generation of intelligence; these models extend its benefits by making that intelligence more efficient and accessible,” the company writes.

The first models in the Sol and Luna series were introduced earlier this year, representing different tiers in OpenAI’s hierarchy of models. Sol is designed for complex tasks like coding, while OpenAI says Luna is more appropriate for clerical work — “high-volume tasks with a clear goal, like summarizing documents, extracting information, or answering quick questions.”

OpenAI is also emphasizing big improvements in efficiency and affordability — most notably, via a substantial price drop for API access. The 6 series models will be available at half the cost of the 5.6 series of Sol and Luna, a price drop that OpenAI attributes to improvements in caching and inference.

OpenAI also claims that its newest models are better at producing answers that are factually accurate, and notes that they have a lower error rate when it comes to coding.

“On our internal factuality evaluation, which is based on de-identified real-world conversations where users flagged mistakes by our models, GPT-6 Sol makes about half as many mistakes as its predecessor, reaching Astra-level reliability at much lower cost,” the announcement reads.

As is typical with OpenAI’s new model releases, the company is claiming that its newest offerings outshine those of its primary competitor, Anthropic. The company repeatedly claims that GPT-6 Sol and Luna handle tasks substantially better than Anthropic’s top models — like Fable and Opus.

Notably, Anthropic released a new version of Opus 5.5 just 90 minutes before OpenAI’s release, reflecting the intense competition between the two companies.

The new versions of Sol and Luna are now available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for most paid accounts, and in the ChatGPT API, while Luna will be available in the desktop app and for Free and Go users. OpenAI expects to roll out the models to ChatGPT (the app and website) gradually throughout the day.

See All by Gaby Del Valle

San Francisco is suing the Trump Media & Technology Group, the parent company behind Truth Social, for selling early access to President Donald Trump’s posts on the social media site. The lawsuit, filed today in California state court, alleges that the Truth API feed is a “corrupt business scheme” that violates both California’s Unfair Competition Law and federal ethics and anti-corruption laws that prohibit insider trading.

White House spokesperson Davis Ingle recently called Truth Social the “most powerful and popular social media platform in the world.” While the latter part of that statement is objectively untrue based on any credible estimates — in fact, Truth Social traffic has declined over the last year — Trump often makes high-stakes announcements in his capacity as president on the platform, and his posts there have a clear effect on the global economy. To capitalize on this, Trump Media recently launched Truth API, a service that charges select customers $100,000 a month for early access to the 10 most influential accounts on Truth Social, including Trump’s and those of other White House officials. Trump Media’s interim CEO, Kevin McGurn, acknowledged as much in his announcement of Truth API, saying that “markets already move on Truth Social posts.”

The San Francisco lawsuit cites several examples of this, some of which took place after the launch of Truth API. On August 21st, for example, Trump posted that the federal government was going to “lower the price of ground beef for working families” by exempting some ground beef imports from tariffs. When the market opened a few hours later, cattle futures declined significantly, according to the complaint.

In today’s markets, early access means millions of dollars. This business scheme has turned public trust into private property.

“Trump Media has unlawfully created, priced, marketed, and operated a commercial mechanism that knowingly and willfully facilitates Trump’s use of nonpublic information for private profit,” the complaint alleges. The San Francisco suit alleges that Truth API is a way of making the floundering Trump Media — which reported a net loss of more than $238 million earlier this year — profitable.

Per his agreement with Trump Media, Truth Social has a six-hour exclusivity window on Trump’s posts, meaning he can’t post the same material elsewhere in that time frame. Even before the launch of Truth API, Trump’s Truth Social profile was extremely valuable for investors — so valuable that the company has sought to capitalize on it. The San Francisco complaint cites reports of hedge fund executives who say they feel pressured to buy the service even though they think it’s legally risky. “It’s a pay-to-play scheme for early access to the president’s market-moving government statements,” San Francisco city attorney David Chiu said in a Tuesday press conference. “In today’s markets, early access means millions of dollars. This business scheme has turned public trust into private property.” Beyond violating insider trading laws, the suit claims, Truth API disadvantages everyday investors by paywalling financially valuable information.

Trump Media hasn’t disclosed its list of Truth API clients, but the company has said it plans on marketing the product to AI companies and large news organizations.

The city has asked a judge to forbid Trump Media from offering Truth API or similar services, and to impose a fine of $2,500 per violation of California’s Unfair Competition Law.

This isn’t the first time Trump has been sued over Truth API. In August, The Intercept and the Freedom of the Press Foundation filed a joint lawsuit in a New York federal court over the product, which it called “extraordinary, corrupt, and unconstitutional.”

旧金山市正起诉特朗普媒体与科技集团（Trump Media & Technology Group），即社交平台Truth Social背后的母公司，原因是该公司出售总统唐纳德·特朗普在这一社交媒体网站上所发布帖文的提前获取权限。这起诉讼于今天在加利福尼亚州法院提起，指控Truth API信息流是一项“腐败的商业计划”，既违反加州《不正当竞争法》，也违反禁止内幕交易的联邦道德和反腐败法律。

白宫发言人戴维斯·英格尔最近称Truth Social是“世界上最强大、最受欢迎的社交媒体平台”。然而，根据任何可信的估算，后半句说法在客观上并不属实——事实上，Truth Social的流量在过去一年有所下降。但特朗普经常以总统身份在该平台上发布具有重大影响力的消息，而他在那里发布的帖子显然会对全球经济产生影响。为了从中获利，特朗普媒体公司最近推出了Truth API。这项服务每月向特定客户收取10万美元，让他们提前获取Truth Social上影响力最大的10个账户的内容，其中包括特朗普以及其他白宫官员的账户。特朗普媒体公司的临时首席执行官凯文·麦格恩在宣布Truth API时也承认了这一点，他说：“市场已经会因Truth Social上的帖子而波动。”

旧金山的诉讼列举了多个相关例子，其中一些发生在Truth API推出之后。例如，8月21日，特朗普发帖称，联邦政府将通过免除部分碎牛肉进口产品的关税，来“降低工薪家庭购买碎牛肉的价格”。诉状称，几小时后市场开盘时，牛类期货价格大幅下跌。

在如今的市场中，提前获取信息意味着数百万美元。这项商业计划把公众信任变成了私人财产。

诉状称：“特朗普媒体公司非法创设、定价、营销并运营了一种商业机制，明知并故意促成特朗普利用非公开信息谋取私利。”旧金山方面的诉讼称，Truth API旨在让陷入困境的特朗普媒体公司实现盈利；该公司今年早些时候公布的净亏损超过2.38亿美元。

根据特朗普媒体公司与特朗普达成的协议，Truth Social对特朗普的帖子拥有6小时的独家发布窗口，这意味着特朗普在这段时间内不能在其他地方发布相同内容。即使在Truth API推出之前，特朗普的Truth Social个人资料对投资者而言就已极具价值——价值之高，以至于该公司一直在寻求从中获利。旧金山的诉状援引了对冲基金高管的相关报道，这些高管表示，尽管认为购买这项服务存在法律风险，他们仍感到有压力必须购买。旧金山市检察官戴维·丘在周二的新闻发布会上说：“这是一个花钱购买提前获取总统具有市场影响力的政府声明权限的交易计划。在如今的市场中，提前获取信息意味着数百万美元。这项商业计划把公众信任变成了私人财产。”诉讼称，Truth API不仅违反内幕交易法，还通过对具有金融价值的信息设置付费墙，使普通投资者处于不利地位。

特朗普媒体公司尚未披露Truth API客户名单，但该公司表示，计划向人工智能公司和大型新闻机构营销这款产品。

旧金山市已请求法官禁止特朗普媒体公司提供Truth API或类似服务，并针对每一项违反加州《不正当竞争法》的行为处以2500美元罚款。

这并不是特朗普第一次因Truth API遭到起诉。今年8月，《拦截》（The Intercept）和新闻自由基金会（Freedom of the Press Foundation）曾在纽约一家联邦法院就这项产品联合提起诉讼，称该产品“非同寻常、腐败且违宪”。

The spokesperson said it will offer teen accounts in cities where its operations are mature and local regulations allow it.

Nashville is a relatively new market for Waymo, although it has support from local leaders to offer the service to teens. The company launched its service in a 50-square-mile area of Nashville in April 2026, and earlier this month, its robotaxis became available on the Lyft app.

Waymo’s ridership has skyrocketed over the past two years — a trajectory largely driven by the rapid succession of new markets. Paid robotaxi trips grew tenfold from 50,000 per week in May 2024 to more than half-a-million per week earlier this year. Over that same time span, Waymo has launched robotaxi services in a dozen cities. In the past month alone, the company opened robotaxi services in Denver, Las Vegas, San Diego, and Tampa.

The company’s introduction of teen accounts provides another means of growth — this one targeted at a demographic that relies on parents or public transit to get to school, work, or activities.

There are few limits to the service. The teen account must be connected to a parent or guardian, but once activated, teens can hail autonomous rides anywhere in Waymo’s service area in Nashville — and bring their friends along. Waymo told TechCrunch that teen account holders can bring up to three guests ages 13 to 17. The company didn’t share how these ages would be verified.

That kind of access could certainly invite chaos — it’s not hard to imagine four 16-year-old kids unleashed in a robotaxi. But it may also be part of the appeal for parents who would rather their kids pile into a Waymo than in a vehicle driven by a teenager.

The Horowitz Andreessen Academy trades degrees and homework for stints at tech companies.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Emma Roth

Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) is creating an “academy” positioned as a pipeline for young people to build or join a Silicon Valley startup. The “Horowitz Andreessen Academy” will launch with 10 partners, including Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe, along with $42 million in funding led by a16z. While billed as a “highly selective school,” it does not grant any degree or accreditation. Instead, students will attend short classes led by tech figureheads, like OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, as well as “co-ops” that give students roles at tech companies.

To partake in the one-year program, students will have to move to San Francisco and arrange their own housing, according to the academy’s FAQ page. Students are promised more than $50,000 in compute credits and a $5,000 travel and research budget offered by a16z. The announcement says they’ll have “no traditional grades, tests, or homework,” but will “learn from Silicon Valley’s most storied founders and operators in short, high-impact classes and spend the rest of your time working and exploring.”

The academy seems like the latest attempt by Silicon Valley’s billionaires to “fix” America’s education system by creating their own. Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Jeff Bezos have all poured money into starting their own schools, while a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz have been critical of colleges. Last year, Andreessen reportedly called Stanford and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology “political lobbying operations fighting American innovation” in a group chat with White House officials and tech leaders, according to The Washington Post.

The Horowitz Andreessen Academy will be free for its first one-year program in the fall of 2027. It will only accept 50 students and is designed mainly for recent high school graduates.

financeStories.snippet: Anthropic called it "the strongest-performing model we've tested to date."
financeStories.fullContent:
Anthropic’s newest model, Opus 5.5, was released on Tuesday, setting a new state-of-the-art in coding and knowledge work performance, according to the company. Opus is the most capable and expensive tier in Anthropic’s three-tier Claude lineup; Sonnet sits in the middle, while Haiku is the fastest and cheapest. Notably, Anthropic says, the release outpaces the larger Fable model in many benchmarks and succeeded in a number of informal tasks that Fable failed to complete.

The new model is also significantly cheaper than its predecessor. Output tokens will be charged at $20 per million tokens for Opus 5.5, compared to $25 for the previous model. Other metrics have similar price drops. The model is also faster to run, reflecting an overall drop in the compute required to serve it.

The new version also makes significant changes to how Opus communicates, with the Opus 5.5 less likely to use jargon and more likely to put important information at the start of its messages.

The launch comes just two months after the release of Opus 5 on July 24. According to the announcement, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, which are the next tiers in the lineup, will be released “in the coming weeks,” with similar performance improvements.

Anthropic says that Opus 5.5 is comparable to Mythos in its biology and cybersecurity capabilities, so its release is subject to the same safeguards as the company’s Fable model. Those safeguards limit how much the models can be used to discover exploits in compiled programs or developing recognizable biological weapons, among other tasks.

Opus 5.5 is Anthropic’s first model release since CEO Dario Amodei embraced calls to pace the frontier, deliberately slowing down progress on AI capabilities to match the rate of progress on alignment.

“I have become convinced that fully addressing the risks requires even more prudence,” Amodei wrote in a post earlier this month, “not just investing in risk prevention, but pacing the rate of capabilities advancement so that risk prevention has time to keep up.”

Opus 5.5’s safety training was broadly similar to its predecessors, with alignment testing and pre-release evaluation by outside organizations like METR and Frontier Design. But Anthropic emphasized that more advanced training and evaluation systems were already being prepared for future models, including improved security and monitoring systems.

“As AI becomes more capable, public policy should play a larger role in making sure the systems people rely on are safe. That capacity takes time to build, and we’ve started to put the infrastructure in place to support it,” the blog post reads. “We expect to share more details on these efforts soon.”

aiStories.originalTitle: Hacking group ShinyHunters claims it breached the FBI, stole agents’ and applicants’ data
aiStories.snippet: The theft of agents' personal information could present a major counterintelligence threat, where agents and their families are extorted into cooperating with a foreign government.
aiStories.fullContent:
ShinyHunters, a prolific cybercriminal group known for large-scale data theft and extortion, says it has breached the FBI and stolen data on thousands of agents and applicants. The hackers made the claim on their dark web leak site, which TechCrunch reviewed, saying they had stolen “sensitive data on almost all FBI agents and individuals who filed an application with the FBI for a job.”

404 Media first reported on the breach after receiving a sample of the stolen names, home addresses, and phone numbers of FBI agents and their spouses, and verifying a portion of the stolen data against public records. The hackers say their hack is “not financially motivated,” and are demanding that the FBI remove a report that they say contains false allegations about the group.

The independent publication said the hackers breached an Oracle PeopleSoft server, often used by human resources and recruiters to store job applicants’ personal information, then pivoted to breach an Amazon-hosted government cloud storing the agents and applicants’ data.

ShinyHunters told the publication that they took terabytes of data but did not say what they would do with the information if the FBI does not take down its published report. The stolen data could present a major counterintelligence threat, in which hackers and overseas spies use the information to coerce or extort FBI agents and their families into cooperating with a foreign government.

The hackers reportedly defaced the FBI’s jobs site, which showed at the time of publication that the portal was “currently down for maintenance.” The site also said that the FBI’s special agent applicant portal was also down.

The FBI did not respond to a request for comment about the incident on Tuesday, and neither did the ShinyHunters hackers.

This is the second known breach of an FBI system this year after unidentified hackers broke into one of the agency’s systems for managing real-time wiretaps and foreign intelligence-gathering warrants, which could have identified targets of the agency’s surveillance. Separately, FBI director Kash Patel also had his personal email account hacked and leaked by an Iran-backed hacking group called Handala in retaliation for U.S.-led strikes against Iran.

aiStories.title: A16z通过创办学校，挑战硅谷对辍学生的偏爱
aiStories.originalTitle: A16z is challenging Silicon Valley’s love for drop-outs by launching a school
aiStories.snippet: This academy for promising high school grads is somewhere between a trade-school, Y Combinator and Peter Thiel's Fellowship Program.
aiStories.fullContent:
Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz is launching a school called The Horowitz Andreessen Academy aimed at aspiring founders who have just graduated high school and have not yet attended college.

The academy is aiming to train these high school grads with hands-on coursework on a variety of topics ranging from the technical (such as “AI Research and Models”) to life philosophy (such as “The Geometry of Luck,” which promises to teach students “about arranging a life so good fortune flows through it.”) Students will also work on personal projects. The school’s main pitch is that it promises to provide students with mentors who are big names in tech.

The school is currently accepting applications for its first year, which will be a one-year program that charges no tuition, and is open to about 50 students, “chosen on proof of work: what they have built, shipped, or earned,” according to the school’s FAQ. The academy is located in San Francisco and students will be responsible for their own housing (although the school is working to help them find it and match them with other student roommates).

One item to note: the academy is currently not an accredited school, so participates will not earn a degree, or college credits that transfer elsewhere.

In 2028, The Horowitz Andreessen Academy — which is a for-profit venture that has raised $42 million — hopes to offer a two-year program. At that point, it plans to charge tuition “similar in cost to an elite private university,” the school’s CEO Gagan Biyani said in a post on X.

In exchange for that elite-tuition price tag, students will gain access to 200 speakers and mentors, including people from ten founding corporate partners: Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe. Those companies and dozens of others hope to hire from the grads of this school, Biyani said.

So, this is like if Y Combinator (the most famed startup school) and Peter Thiel’s Fellowship Program (a famed program for young people who opt to build companies instead of attend college) had a baby. The difference is, instead of a short-term experience ending with funding for a company, these students will pay tuition, earn tech-trade skills and have an inside track at tech industry jobs. Or they may also have a startup in the works, built with access to a lot of mentorship.

As the founders of the academy describe, it’s meant to be a new, middle ground between obtaining a full degree before entering the tech industry and dropping out to start a company. In this era where AI has been hampering the entry-level job market, gaining access to jobs may enough reason for some young people to try this new trade-school like approach.

The Touch ID functionality is compatible with macOS computers running version 15.1 or newer on Apple-made silicon.

The keyboard includes a woven USB-C cable that handles both charging and data, or you can use Bluetooth for a wireless connection. Black-colored Apple accessories tend to carry a higher price premium than their equivalent white models, and go on sale less frequently. Best Buy’s price is only good through 10PM PT on September 22nd, 2026, and the Amazon page is currently shipping one or two days out.

This compact charger sports three USB-C ports, with a maximum output of 140W from a single port. It even has a little display for power monitoring or changing charging modes with the push of a button.

For a limited time, you can grab a 512GB microSD Express card for $99.99 or less. The Samsung P9 is $99.99 at B&H Photo and Amazon (discounted automatically applied at checkout), and the SanDisk GamePlay is $98 at Walmart . The Switch 2 is the only mainstream device that requires a microSD Express for add-ons torage, and first-party Nintendo games run between 10 and 30 GB (the upcoming Ocarina of time remake is 27GB, for example) so a 512GB card can store upwards of 15 games.

The 4K Blu-ray version of Interstellar is discounted to $14.96 at Amazon . That’s the lowest we’ve seen the price since Prime Day in June, and a five dollar break from the usual price. aiStories.title: OpenAI推出GPT-6 Sol和Luna，主打更低成本与更少错误
aiStories.originalTitle: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna, boasting lower cost and fewer mistakes
aiStories.snippet: OpenAI is launching two new models, which it says are cut from the same cloth as Astra.
aiStories.fullContent:
Earlier this month, OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra, which it heralded as its most powerful and capable model yet, and the “world’s best model” for a variety of activities, including computer work and coding. Now, the lab is expanding the GPT-6 generation with updated versions of the smaller Sol and Luna models.

“GPT-6 Astra introduced a new generation of intelligence; these models extend its benefits by making that intelligence more efficient and accessible,” the company writes.

The first models in the Sol and Luna series were introduced earlier this year, representing different tiers in OpenAI’s hierarchy of models. Sol is designed for complex tasks like coding, while OpenAI says Luna is more appropriate for clerical work — “high-volume tasks with a clear goal, like summarizing documents, extracting information, or answering quick questions.”

OpenAI is also emphasizing big improvements in efficiency and affordability — most notably, via a substantial price drop for API access. The 6 series models will be available at half the cost of the 5.6 series of Sol and Luna, a price drop that OpenAI attributes to improvements in caching and inference.

OpenAI also claims that its newest models are better at producing answers that are factually accurate, and notes that they have a lower error rate when it comes to coding.

“On our internal factuality evaluation, which is based on de-identified real-world conversations where users flagged mistakes by our models, GPT-6 Sol makes about half as many mistakes as its predecessor, reaching Astra-level reliability at much lower cost,” the announcement reads.

As is typical with OpenAI’s new model releases, the company is claiming that its newest offerings outshine those of its primary competitor, Anthropic. The company repeatedly claims that GPT-6 Sol and Luna handle tasks substantially better than Anthropic’s top models — like Fable and Opus.

Notably, Anthropic released a new version of Opus 5.5 just 90 minutes before OpenAI’s release, reflecting the intense competition between the two companies.

The new versions of Sol and Luna are now available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for most paid accounts, and in the ChatGPT API, while Luna will be available in the desktop app and for Free and Go users. OpenAI expects to roll out the models to ChatGPT (the app and website) gradually throughout the day.

See All by Gaby Del Valle

San Francisco is suing the Trump Media & Technology Group, the parent company behind Truth Social, for selling early access to President Donald Trump’s posts on the social media site. The lawsuit, filed today in California state court, alleges that the Truth API feed is a “corrupt business scheme” that violates both California’s Unfair Competition Law and federal ethics and anti-corruption laws that prohibit insider trading.

White House spokesperson Davis Ingle recently called Truth Social the “most powerful and popular social media platform in the world.” While the latter part of that statement is objectively untrue based on any credible estimates — in fact, Truth Social traffic has declined over the last year — Trump often makes high-stakes announcements in his capacity as president on the platform, and his posts there have a clear effect on the global economy. To capitalize on this, Trump Media recently launched Truth API, a service that charges select customers $100,000 a month for early access to the 10 most influential accounts on Truth Social, including Trump’s and those of other White House officials. Trump Media’s interim CEO, Kevin McGurn, acknowledged as much in his announcement of Truth API, saying that “markets already move on Truth Social posts.”

The San Francisco lawsuit cites several examples of this, some of which took place after the launch of Truth API. On August 21st, for example, Trump posted that the federal government was going to “lower the price of ground beef for working families” by exempting some ground beef imports from tariffs. When the market opened a few hours later, cattle futures declined significantly, according to the complaint.

In today’s markets, early access means millions of dollars. This business scheme has turned public trust into private property.

“Trump Media has unlawfully created, priced, marketed, and operated a commercial mechanism that knowingly and willfully facilitates Trump’s use of nonpublic information for private profit,” the complaint alleges. The San Francisco suit alleges that Truth API is a way of making the floundering Trump Media — which reported a net loss of more than $238 million earlier this year — profitable.

Per his agreement with Trump Media, Truth Social has a six-hour exclusivity window on Trump’s posts, meaning he can’t post the same material elsewhere in that time frame. Even before the launch of Truth API, Trump’s Truth Social profile was extremely valuable for investors — so valuable that the company has sought to capitalize on it. The San Francisco complaint cites reports of hedge fund executives who say they feel pressured to buy the service even though they think it’s legally risky. “It’s a pay-to-play scheme for early access to the president’s market-moving government statements,” San Francisco city attorney David Chiu said in a Tuesday press conference. “In today’s markets, early access means millions of dollars. This business scheme has turned public trust into private property.” Beyond violating insider trading laws, the suit claims, Truth API disadvantages everyday investors by paywalling financially valuable information.

Trump Media hasn’t disclosed its list of Truth API clients, but the company has said it plans on marketing the product to AI companies and large news organizations.

The city has asked a judge to forbid Trump Media from offering Truth API or similar services, and to impose a fine of $2,500 per violation of California’s Unfair Competition Law.

This isn’t the first time Trump has been sued over Truth API. In August, The Intercept and the Freedom of the Press Foundation filed a joint lawsuit in a New York federal court over the product, which it called “extraordinary, corrupt, and unconstitutional.”

旧金山市指控特朗普媒体公司为内幕交易提供便利。

这位作者发布的帖子将被添加到您的每日电子邮件摘要和首页信息流中。

查看Gaby Del Valle发布的全部内容

旧金山市正起诉特朗普媒体与科技集团（Trump Media & Technology Group），即社交平台Truth Social背后的母公司，原因是该公司出售总统唐纳德·特朗普在这一社交媒体网站上所发布帖文的提前获取权限。这起诉讼于今天在加利福尼亚州法院提起，指控Truth API信息流是一项“腐败的商业计划”，既违反加州《不正当竞争法》，也违反禁止内幕交易的联邦道德和反腐败法律。

白宫发言人戴维斯·英格尔最近称Truth Social是“世界上最强大、最受欢迎的社交媒体平台”。然而，根据任何可信的估算，后半句说法在客观上并不属实——事实上，Truth Social的流量在过去一年有所下降。但特朗普经常以总统身份在该平台上发布具有重大影响力的消息，而他在那里发布的帖子显然会对全球经济产生影响。为了从中获利，特朗普媒体公司最近推出了Truth API。这项服务每月向特定客户收取10万美元，让他们提前获取Truth Social上影响力最大的10个账户的内容，其中包括特朗普以及其他白宫官员的账户。特朗普媒体公司的临时首席执行官凯文·麦格恩在宣布Truth API时也承认了这一点，他说：“市场已经会因Truth Social上的帖子而波动。”

旧金山的诉讼列举了多个相关例子，其中一些发生在Truth API推出之后。例如，8月21日，特朗普发帖称，联邦政府将通过免除部分碎牛肉进口产品的关税，来“降低工薪家庭购买碎牛肉的价格”。诉状称，几小时后市场开盘时，牛类期货价格大幅下跌。

在如今的市场中，提前获取信息意味着数百万美元。这项商业计划把公众信任变成了私人财产。

诉状称：“特朗普媒体公司非法创设、定价、营销并运营了一种商业机制，明知并故意促成特朗普利用非公开信息谋取私利。”旧金山方面的诉讼称，Truth API旨在让陷入困境的特朗普媒体公司实现盈利；该公司今年早些时候公布的净亏损超过2.38亿美元。

根据特朗普媒体公司与特朗普达成的协议，Truth Social对特朗普的帖子拥有6小时的独家发布窗口，这意味着特朗普在这段时间内不能在其他地方发布相同内容。即使在Truth API推出之前，特朗普的Truth Social个人资料对投资者而言就已极具价值——价值之高，以至于该公司一直在寻求从中获利。旧金山的诉状援引了对冲基金高管的相关报道，这些高管表示，尽管认为购买这项服务存在法律风险，他们仍感到有压力必须购买。旧金山市检察官戴维·丘在周二的新闻发布会上说：“这是一个花钱购买提前获取总统具有市场影响力的政府声明权限的交易计划。在如今的市场中，提前获取信息意味着数百万美元。这项商业计划把公众信任变成了私人财产。”诉讼称，Truth API不仅违反内幕交易法，还通过对具有金融价值的信息设置付费墙，使普通投资者处于不利地位。

aiStories.snippet: Waymo is opening its robotaxi service to teenagers aged 13 to 17 in Nashville, its second city to offer rides to minors.
aiStories.fullContent:
Waymo will allow teenagers as young as 13 to use its robotaxi service in Nashville as the Alphabet-owned company looks to scale its business by reaching a new group of riders.

Nashville is the second city to offer Waymo teen accounts; the company kicked off its teen account program in Phoenix last year. And more cities are likely to follow, according to the company.

A Waymo spokesperson told TechCrunch that its expansion to Nashville will be the “first of many” teen launches across multiple markets that use the Waymo app in the coming months. The spokesperson said it will offer teen accounts in cities where its operations are mature and local regulations allow it.

Nashville is a relatively new market for Waymo, although it has support from local leaders to offer the service to teens. The company launched its service in a 50-square-mile area of Nashville in April 2026, and earlier this month, its robotaxis became available on the Lyft app.

Waymo’s ridership has skyrocketed over the past two years — a trajectory largely driven by the rapid succession of new markets. Paid robotaxi trips grew tenfold from 50,000 per week in May 2024 to more than half-a-million per week earlier this year. Over that same time span, Waymo has launched robotaxi services in a dozen cities. In the past month alone, the company opened robotaxi services in Denver, Las Vegas, San Diego, and Tampa.

The company’s introduction of teen accounts provides another means of growth — this one targeted at a demographic that relies on parents or public transit to get to school, work, or activities.

There are few limits to the service. The teen account must be connected to a parent or guardian, but once activated, teens can hail autonomous rides anywhere in Waymo’s service area in Nashville — and bring their friends along. Waymo told TechCrunch that teen account holders can bring up to three guests ages 13 to 17. The company didn’t share how these ages would be verified.

That kind of access could certainly invite chaos — it’s not hard to imagine four 16-year-old kids unleashed in a robotaxi. But it may also be part of the appeal for parents who would rather their kids pile into a Waymo than in a vehicle driven by a teenager.

The Horowitz Andreessen Academy trades degrees and homework for stints at tech companies.

Venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) is creating an “academy” positioned as a pipeline for young people to build or join a Silicon Valley startup. The “Horowitz Andreessen Academy” will launch with 10 partners, including Anduril, Anthropic, Coinbase, Google, Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit, and Stripe, along with $42 million in funding led by a16z. While billed as a “highly selective school,” it does not grant any degree or accreditation. Instead, students will attend short classes led by tech figureheads, like OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, as well as “co-ops” that give students roles at tech companies.

To partake in the one-year program, students will have to move to San Francisco and arrange their own housing, according to the academy’s FAQ page. Students are promised more than $50,000 in compute credits and a $5,000 travel and research budget offered by a16z. The announcement says they’ll have “no traditional grades, tests, or homework,” but will “learn from Silicon Valley’s most storied founders and operators in short, high-impact classes and spend the rest of your time working and exploring.”

The academy seems like the latest attempt by Silicon Valley’s billionaires to “fix” America’s education system by creating their own. Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, and Jeff Bezos have all poured money into starting their own schools, while a16z founders Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz have been critical of colleges. Last year, Andreessen reportedly called Stanford and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology “political lobbying operations fighting American innovation” in a group chat with White House officials and tech leaders, according to The Washington Post.

The Horowitz Andreessen Academy will be free for its first one-year program in the fall of 2027. It will only accept 50 students and is designed mainly for recent high school graduates.

aiStories.fullContent:
Anthropic’s newest model, Opus 5.5, was released on Tuesday, setting a new state-of-the-art in coding and knowledge work performance, according to the company. Opus is the most capable and expensive tier in Anthropic’s three-tier Claude lineup; Sonnet sits in the middle, while Haiku is the fastest and cheapest. Notably, Anthropic says, the release outpaces the larger Fable model in many benchmarks and succeeded in a number of informal tasks that Fable failed to complete.

The new model is also significantly cheaper than its predecessor. Output tokens will be charged at $20 per million tokens for Opus 5.5, compared to $25 for the previous model. Other metrics have similar price drops. The model is also faster to run, reflecting an overall drop in the compute required to serve it.

The new version also makes significant changes to how Opus communicates, with the Opus 5.5 less likely to use jargon and more likely to put important information at the start of its messages.

The launch comes just two months after the release of Opus 5 on July 24. According to the announcement, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, which are the next tiers in the lineup, will be released “in the coming weeks,” with similar performance improvements.

Anthropic says that Opus 5.5 is comparable to Mythos in its biology and cybersecurity capabilities, so its release is subject to the same safeguards as the company’s Fable model. Those safeguards limit how much the models can be used to discover exploits in compiled programs or developing recognizable biological weapons, among other tasks.

Opus 5.5 is Anthropic’s first model release since CEO Dario Amodei embraced calls to pace the frontier, deliberately slowing down progress on AI capabilities to match the rate of progress on alignment.

“I have become convinced that fully addressing the risks requires even more prudence,” Amodei wrote in a post earlier this month, “not just investing in risk prevention, but pacing the rate of capabilities advancement so that risk prevention has time to keep up.”

Opus 5.5’s safety training was broadly similar to its predecessors, with alignment testing and pre-release evaluation by outside organizations like METR and Frontier Design. But Anthropic emphasized that more advanced training and evaluation systems were already being prepared for future models, including improved security and monitoring systems.

“As AI becomes more capable, public policy should play a larger role in making sure the systems people rely on are safe. That capacity takes time to build, and we’ve started to put the infrastructure in place to support it,” the blog post reads. “We expect to share more details on these efforts soon.”

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Emma Roth

Anthropic says its new Claude Opus 5.5 model comes with stronger safeguards in the wake of recent rogue AI hacking incidents. In an announcement on Tuesday, Anthropic says Opus 5.5 comes with improvements to certain risky behaviors, including attempts to escape the company’s testing sandbox.

It’s the first model released by Anthropic after CEO Dario Amodei announced plans to “pace the frontier,” or slow down AI development. In recent weeks, several AI companies, including Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, have reported that their AI models escaped containment and hacked third-party companies during testing.

Anthropic says Opus 5.5 is the “strongest-performing” model on the company’s most comprehensive alignment test. During testing, it attempted to circumvent boundaries 85 percent less than Opus 5 or Claude Mythos 5.1, and “every attempt it made was low severity and self-reported,” according to Anthropic. It also comes with improvements to biased or motivated reasoning, which contributed to recent AI hacks.

Opus 5.5 costs 40 percent less to run than Opus 5, but matches the performance of Fable 5.1 “on most work.” It also comes with safeguards similar to the ones offered by Anthropic’s more advanced Fable 5.1 model. That means Opus 5.5 will re-route certain cybersecurity-related requests to the less powerful Opus 4.8, while biology-related requests flagged by its safeguards will go to Opus 5.

Anthropic says Opus 5.5 was tested by outside partners, including Frontier Design and METR, before release. The company also plans to launch Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 in the coming weeks.

trendStories.fullContent:
Providing psychological safety to Black, Asian and ethnic minority staff so they can raise concerns about patient care without fear would save lives, write Dr Jennifer Creese, Dr Joy Spiliopoulos and Prof Carolyn Tarrant

Your report ( One in five black, Asian and minority ethnic NHS managers in England plan to quit amid racism, report finds, 15 September ) rightly highlights racism, exclusion and blocked career progression in the NHS. But it also points to a wider risk: patient safety. Care mistakes already cost the NHS £14.7bn a year .

A March 2025 report by the NHS Race & Health Observatory notes that Black, Asian and minority ethnic (BAME) staff, who make up more than 40% of the medical and dental workforce, still face harassment and discrimination in promotion, everyday work and disciplinary processes. This fuels stress, burnout and poorer mental health. Bullying and harassment are estimated to cost NHS England £2bn a year through staff turnover, sickness and lost productivity. In such environments, BAME staff are less likely than white colleagues to speak up about patient safety, fearing that their concerns will not be understood or taken seriously.

詹妮弗·克里斯博士（Dr Jennifer Creese）、乔伊·斯皮利奥普洛斯博士（Dr Joy Spiliopoulos）和卡罗琳·塔兰特教授（Prof Carolyn Tarrant）写道，为黑人、亚裔和少数族裔员工提供心理安全保障，使他们能够毫无畏惧地提出对患者护理的担忧，将挽救生命。

贵报的报道（《报告发现：在英格兰，五分之一的黑人、亚裔及少数族裔NHS管理者因种族主义计划辞职》，9月15日）准确指出了英国国家医疗服务体系（NHS）内部存在的种族主义、排斥以及职业发展受阻问题。但这同时也指向了一个更广泛的风险：患者安全。医疗差错每年已给NHS造成高达147亿英镑的损失。

NHS种族与健康观察机构（NHS Race & Health Observatory）2025年3月的一份报告指出，在医疗和牙科从业人员中占比超过40%的黑人、亚裔和少数族裔（BAME）员工，在晋升、日常工作以及纪律处分程序中仍面临骚扰与歧视。这加剧了心理压力、职业倦怠以及较差的心理健康状况。据估计，欺凌和骚扰通过导致人员流失、病假和生产力下降，每年给英格兰NHS造成20亿英镑的损失。在这样的环境下，少数族裔员工比白人同事更不愿意公开谈论患者安全问题，他们担心自己的关切不会被理解或受到重视。

trendStories.fullContent:
In more than two decades in the Prison Service, Pia Sinha gained a reputation as a fixer. Now, as head of the Prison Reform Trust, she’s sounding the alarm about overcrowding and other problems

Pia Sinha has led the Prison Reform Trust since 2023. In that time, she has seen a Conservative government finally admit to an overcrowding crisis that had tipped over the edge. (It was in October 2023 that the early release scheme was devised; by May 2024, the Tories had also launched Operation Safeguard , using police cells as temporary housing.) She’s watched a change of government, then a change of prime minister, then Andy Burnham instantly assailed by negative headlines as the consequences of that early release scheme unfolded: prisoners had to actually be released early. “We’re a bit concerned about how [Burnham] has handled it,” she says, in the trust’s scruffy, un-corporate offices in central London, “but that’s in the knowledge that he had a bit of a hospital pass.”

To recap on Burnham’s handling: when he came in in July, he paused the scheme for an urgent review; in August he announced a series of exclusions, further crimes for which people couldn’t be released early, including manslaughter and death by dangerous driving. That solved an immediate problem, that the killers of PC Andrew Harper would otherwise have been released, but had the knock-on effect of reducing the numbers expected to be released by about a quarter. The conversation Sinha wants to have is what prison overcrowding looks like, what it does to prisoners and staff – and what it means for society.
trendStories.fullTranslation:
在监狱系统任职的二十多年里，皮娅·辛哈（Pia Sinha）赢得了“解决问题能手”的声誉。如今，作为监狱改革信托基金会（Prison Reform Trust）的负责人，她正对过度拥挤及其他问题敲响警钟。

自2023年以来，皮娅·辛哈一直领导着监狱改革信托基金会。在此期间，她见证了保守党政府终于承认监狱过度拥挤危机已经濒临失控。（正是在2023年10月，提前释放计划得以制定；到2024年5月，保守党还启动了“保障行动”[Operation Safeguard]，利用警方拘留室作为临时羁押场所。）她目睹了政权更迭，随后首相换人，接着安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）因该提前释放计划后果显现而立刻遭到负面头条新闻的围攻：囚犯实际上不得不被提前释放。“我们对他（伯纳姆）的处理方式感到有点担忧，”她在该信托基金会位于伦敦市中心简陋、毫无企业气派的办公室里说道，“但我们也清楚，他接手的是一个烫手山芋。”

回顾一下伯纳姆的处理方式：他在7月上任时，叫停了该计划以进行紧急审查；8月，他宣布了一系列排除条款，增加了不得提前释放的罪行范围，包括过失杀人以及危险驾驶致人死亡。这解决了一个当务之急，即避免了杀害警官安德鲁·哈珀（PC Andrew Harper）的凶手被提前释放，但其连锁反应是使预计提前释放的人数减少了约四分之一。辛哈希望探讨的是，监狱过度拥挤究竟是何种景象、它对囚犯和工作人员造成了什么影响——以及这对整个社会意味着什么。
